headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from AutoGen-to-OpenMetadata handoff; shared write/network surfaces also create medium conflict and leakage concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute tool calls, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGen outputs are ingested by OpenMetadata or vice versa. The pair lacks documented provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGen outputs are routed into OpenMetadata MCP tools or webhooks without provenance tagging, injection risk is present.
IF OpenMetadata content is later parsed by AutoGen as instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of free-form text between the systems.
Add a provenance prefix to all cross-agent messages.
Restrict OpenMetadata webhook/MCP inputs to structured schemas.
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like payloads before enabling automation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys and can read/write local files; OpenMetadata touches technical metadata, governance, lineage, and memory. If they share a workspace or same principal, sensitive operational metadata can flow into AutoGen outputs or external model calls. The profiles do not show isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace, OpenMetadata metadata can be exposed to AutoGen.
IF AutoGen forwards shared files to model providers, copied metadata can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate working directories immediately.
Remove secrets from shared folders.
Limit AutoGen inputs to redacted extracts.
Audit one outbound request from each system for metadata leakage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and network egress; OpenMetadata has APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Their mutable surfaces overlap on shared resources, but the profiles do not prove same-dir writes or shared locks. Because uncertainty escalates and both can mutate external state, medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or API object, write conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata MCP actions and AutoGen shell actions run concurrently, last-write-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource namespaces.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file or queue.
Disable concurrent edits to shared records.
Test one conflicting update path in a staging workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and OpenMetadata is designed for data collaboration/governance and can act on APIs, events, and webhooks. If OpenMetadata treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream metadata or governance actions. The default interaction is risky enough to rate high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata consumes AutoGen-generated facts without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF AutoGen hallucinates lineage or governance details and OpenMetadata publishes them, the error propagates.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for generated facts.
Require schema validation before OpenMetadata writes.
Mark AutoGen output as untrusted by default.
Compare one generated record against source-of-truth data before rollout.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and application data, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if governed metadata is copied into AutoGen logs or external model calls. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so the risk is compliance-relevant but not provably severe.
conditions: IF governed metadata or secrets are copied into AutoGen prompts, retention policy mismatch is triggered.
IF OpenMetadata stores records subject to deletion/export and AutoGen logs them elsewhere, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Classify shared fields before enabling sync.
Exclude secrets and regulated fields from prompts.
Set a short retention window for cross-agent logs.
Document deletion/export handling for one shared dataset.
